title: Hong Kong court jails Joshua Wong for 10 more years for 'foreign collusion'
dek: The activist, already in custody since 2020, is likely to stay in prison until about 2036. The US condemned the sentence; Beijing told other countries not to interfere.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
A Hong Kong court on Thursday sentenced the pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong to 10 more years in prison for conspiring to collude with foreign forces, his second conviction under the national security law that Beijing imposed on the city in 2020.

Judge William Tam of the High Court said he began from a 13-year starting point and took three years off for Wong's guilty plea, Hong Kong Free Press reported. "Whilst it is a very heavy sentence on the defendant, the punishment must fit the gravity of the crime committed," the judge said. Wong, who turned 30 in prison last month, had been due for release in January, according to the Associated Press. He is now likely to remain in prison until about 2036, Hong Kong Free Press reported, unless he is granted remission.

## What the court found

Prosecutors said Wong conspired with the self-exiled activist Nathan Law and others in 2020 to ask foreign governments to impose sanctions, blockades or other hostile measures on the governments of Hong Kong and mainland China, including by lobbying for laws such as the US Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act. Judge Tam described Wong and Law as the "ring-leaders" and "masterminds", and said their campaign for international sanctions had worsened the political crisis during the 2019 and 2020 protests, Hong Kong Free Press reported. The offence carries a minimum of 10 years.

The new term runs concurrently with the two months left on Wong's earlier sentence of four years and eight months in the "Hong Kong 47" subversion case, the city's largest national security prosecution. He has been in custody since late 2020, first for organising an unauthorised protest outside police headquarters in 2019.

## What each side says

The United States condemned the sentence and called for Wong's immediate release; the US Consulate General in Hong Kong said he had been "unjustly imprisoned" since late 2020, the AP reported. Hong Kong's government said it "strongly condemned and opposed" the consulate spokesman's remarks, according to The Standard, and accused the US of smearing the city's courts.

China's foreign ministry spokesperson, Guo Jiakun, said Wong had pleaded guilty in the face of "overwhelming facts and evidence" and that "relevant parties" should stop interfering in Hong Kong's judiciary, according to the AP. Hong Kong's chief executive, John Lee, called Wong, Law and their accomplices among the "primary culprits" who had undermined the city's prosperity and stability. Steve Li, the chief superintendent of the police national security department, welcomed the ruling and urged Law to return and surrender, Radio Free Asia reported.

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned the sentence as political prosecution and urged Beijing and Hong Kong to free those detained, RFA reported. In the US Congress, John Moolenaar, the Republican chair of the House Select Committee on China, called the charges "baseless". Eric Lai of Georgetown University's Center for Asian Law told the AP that national security charges "can be repeatedly weaponized" to keep a political prisoner in jail.

## Background

Hong Kong and Beijing say the national security law, which criminalises subversion, secession, terrorism and collusion with foreign forces, restored stability after the 2019 protests, and that prosecutions are based on evidence, not political views. The UN human rights office and rights groups have criticised it. In February, the media owner Jimmy Lai was sentenced to 20 years for conspiring to collude with foreign forces, and three former executives of his Apple Daily newspaper received 10-year terms.

## Why it matters

The sentence shows how broadly Hong Kong now applies the foreign collusion offence: the conduct at its centre was lobbying foreign governments and legislatures for sanctions, and the court counted campaigning that began in 2019, before the national security law was imposed, as part of the aggravating background. China's response to the US statement, that other countries should not interfere in Hong Kong's courts, is the position Beijing takes whenever foreign governments raise Hong Kong.
